title: Peak flow at home
what: A peak flow meter is a small device you blow into hard. It shows how open your airways are right now.
why: Mostly for asthma: to track your breathing at home and notice when it gets worse in time.
duration: one measurement takes about a minute, usually morning and evening
tell_doctor: Your personal best result. Your doctor uses it to set your normal range
How often you have attacks or wake up at night
Which inhalers you use, and when

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: It is usually measured morning and evening, at the same times. Your doctor will set the schedule.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: It is usually measured before using your inhaler. Ask your doctor. Do not change your treatment on your own.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Write your results in a notebook or an app.

steps: Set the meter's pointer to zero
Seal your lips tightly around the mouthpiece
Blow out as hard and fast as you can
Repeat 3 times and write down the best result
feel: Sometimes blowing hard causes a cough or slight dizziness
after: Compare your results with your normal range
Show your diary to the doctor at your visit
Your doctor may give you a plan: what to do when your results drop
red_flags: Your result has dropped a lot and the inhaler does not help: call emergency services
It is hard to talk, or your lips turn blue: call emergency services

faq.a: Everyone's normal is different. It is based on your personal best. Your doctor will explain your zones.

faq.q: How many times should I blow?
faq.a: Usually 3 times in a row. Write down the best one.

reminders.text: Remember to measure your peak flow in the morning and write it in your diary.
